title: Fisher-metric distance for task update code assignment
hypothesis: Fisher-weighted Mirror code assignment will preserve heldout functional updates with >=25% fewer complete bytes and lower Fisher-weighted task error/interference than Euclidean assignment, while strictly beating native Fisher k-means controls.

world.teacher: six clustered updates with small isotropic Fisher-whitened residual

development.tuning: none; deterministic farthest-point initialization and Lloyd clustering

fresh.release_rule: Keep fresh sealed after exact native Fisher-control alias or strict gate miss.

success_gate: PASS only if Fisher nRMSE <=0.02, >=25% fewer complete bytes than independent, lower Fisher error than Euclidean assignment, and strict advantage over native Fisher k-means.
failure_gate: FAIL if quality/bytes gate misses or native Fisher k-means matches Mirror without a frontier gain.
boundaries: Synthetic linearized task updates only; no trained PEFT or real Fisher estimator.
Six update clusters are constructed; heldout tasks are samples from known clusters.
No fresh seeds after native control alias or gate miss.
